An R interface to peekbank

The peekbankr package allows you to access data in Peekbank, an open database of developmental eye-tracking data, from R. Data are retrieved from the versioned peekbank dataset on Redivis; the get_ functions return tidy tables without you having to write queries. The package vignette provides examples of the data loading functions and what the resulting data look like.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("peekbank/peekbankr")

The first data request will open a browser window to authorize Redivis access (free account). For non-interactive use, set a REDIVIS_API_TOKEN environment variable instead. That token needs the data.metadata scope.

Usage 

library(tidyverse)
library(peekbankr)

pb <- peekbank("2026.1")   # create a peekbank client with a database version

data <- pb$aoi_timepoints %>%
  left_join(pb$administrations)

This downloads the datasets automatically for the first access and caches them for subsequent use.

If you only want to download a subset of the release, pb$subset$<table>() takes dplyr expressions and returns only the matching rows:

aoi_timepoints <- pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016")
administrations <- pb$subset$administrations(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016")

ps_data <- aoi_timepoints %>%
  left_join(administrations)

Predicates are dplyr expressions. A predicate can name any column of the table, or columns of any table that a row of the queried table is connected to:

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(age >= 24, age <= 36, sex == "female")
pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(vanilla_trial, !excluded)
pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(target_stimulus_novelty == "familiar")
pb$subset$administrations(sex == "female")
pb$subset$trials(vanilla_trial)

These also work across tables:

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016",
                         age < 24 & vanilla_trial)

The exception is t_norm on pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(), as by default we transfers the table run-length encoded (one row per run of a constant AOI) and t_norm filters would result in unintuitive behavior. If you need to filter t_norm, either do it on the fetched result OR pass rle = FALSE to read the expanded table directly (which will make the fetch take a lot longer):

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016", t_norm > 0) # Error

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016", t_norm > 0,
                         rle = FALSE)

Every other column filters normally, including aoi, which is constant within a run. pb$subset$xy_timepoints() is not encoded, so it has no such restriction.

For the timepoint tables, the predicates are translated to remote SQL queries, so only a subset of predicates is available. If you use a predicate that cannot be translated to a query, an error message will let you know. The smaller tables are filtered in R, so they take arbitrary dplyr expression.

Server-side queries

pb$db holds a dbplyr handle on each table. dplyr verbs on it compile to SQL and run on the server; data transfer happens when you collect(). Here is an example that summarises a timepoint table without pulling it:

pb$db$aoi_timepoints %>%
  group_by(aoi) %>%
  count() %>%
  collect()

pb$db also holds aoi_timepoints_rle, one row per run of a constant AOI, for anyone who wants the stored shape rather than the samples it expands to.

Print the client to see the release it is pinned to and what is on it:

pb
#> <peekbank> release 2026.1 (Redivis version v1.4)
#>   tables:  datasets subjects administrations trials trial_types stimuli
#>            aoi_region_sets aoi_timepoints xy_timepoints
#>   methods: clear_cache() download_stimuli() query() readmes()
#>   subset:  $subset$<table>(<dplyr predicates>)
#>   db:      $db$<table> for a dbplyr handle, read on collect()

Database versions

Peekbank is released in named versions (e.g. 2026.1), and peekbank() requires one. get_db_info() lists what is available.

Pass "current" to take whichever version was published most recently for testing, but this is strongly discouraged as future version releases will make the same code produce different results.

pb <- peekbank("2026.1")
pb$release   # "2026.1"

Data files

Raw data, processed intermediates, and per-dataset READMEs live in the companion peekbank_files dataset:

pb$readmes(datasets = "pomper_saffran_2016")       # dataset documentation
stimuli <- pb$download_stimuli(datasets = "reflook_v4")  # stimulus images

Development

After making changes, run roxygen2::roxygenise() to update exports and documentation, and testthat::test_local() for the offline test suite.

Running the full test suite requires Redivis credentials: Without them the network tests skip. Copy .Renviron.template to .Renviron, fill in a personal API token from your Redivis workspace settings, and set PEEKBANK_NETWORK_TESTS=true.
